content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late window, particularly when true values show sharp declines or mean reversion.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history, then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Underreacts to sustained downward trends; forecasts remain too high even when true values are falling.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, especially when history includes recent high values.
- Lags in recognizing true price drops; forecasts remain elevated for 2–3 days after a sharp decline.
- Mean reversion is not captured well; model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price behavior suggests.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven price corrections.
